:::{#def-tangent-plane}
#### Tangent plane

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have a gradient at $\vy$ (@def-vector-derivative).
The **tangent plane** to the [graph](sets-functions.qmd#def-graph) of $f$ at $\vy$
is the graph of the function

$$
\vx \mapsto f(\vy) + \tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} f(\vy)}} (\vx - \vy),
$$

which takes the value $f(\vy)$ at $\vx = \vy$ and has the same gradient as $f$ there.
For $p = 1$ it is the [tangent line](calculus.qmd#def-tangent-line) $s = f(y) + f'(y)\,(x - y)$,
the line through $(y, f(y))$ with slope $f'(y)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-tangent-plane}
#### A tangent line and a tangent plane

- For $f(x) = x^2$ at $y = 1$, $f(1) = 1$ and $f'(1) = 2$, so the tangent line is

  $$
  \ba
  s
  &= 1 + 2\,(x - 1)
  && \text{(substitute } f(1) \text{ and } f'(1) \text{)}
  \\
  &= 1 + 2x - 2
  && \text{(distribute)}
  \\
  &= 2x - 1.
  && \text{(} 1 - 2 = -1 \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

- For $f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^2$ at $\vy = \tp{(1, 1)}$,
  $f(\vy) = 2$ and the gradient is $\tp{(2 y_1,\ 2 y_2)} = \tp{(2, 2)}$, so the tangent plane is

  $$
  \ba
  s
  &= 2 + 2\,(x_1 - 1) + 2\,(x_2 - 1)
  && \text{(substitute } f(\vy) \text{ and the gradient)}
  \\
  &= 2 + 2 x_1 - 2 + 2 x_2 - 2
  && \text{(distribute)}
  \\
  &= 2 x_1 + 2 x_2 - 2.
  && \text{(} 2 - 2 - 2 = -2 \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

:::
